hasPart.name: Areas of practice.
hasPart.text: The studio & venture Areas of practice. The core offering is undivided attention. Close study of the artist, the work, and the conditions shaping both. We observe, listen, and stay with the material long enough to offer a precise response. We scout talent and work with artists directly, or partner with record labels, galleries, and booking agencies. In either case, the artist enters the engagement willingly, on their own initiative or through a representative. Every engagement begins with an agreed scope and an upfront monthly Stewardship subscription or fixed project fee. 01.0 // Sovereign A&R Multidisciplinary Artist & Repertoire: scouting artists and developing complete bodies of work across music, visual art, literature, and film through critique, direction, and critical framing. The artist retains 100% ownership and creative control. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share.

hasPart.name: Retainer terms.
hasPart.text: Our commitment Retainer terms. Focused intervention. Space to execute. The monthly Stewardship subscription keeps studio capacity available between interventions. We come close to observe and edit, then step away while the artist executes on their own timeline. Wild-Lake takes no percentage of artist earnings or ownership of their intellectual property. Scope & deliverables Every retained engagement begins with a fixed-scope architectural proposal. Depending on the artist's stage, deliverables include a written practice audit, a complete repertoire and catalog map, a six-month working rhythm and boundary protocol, or a bare-metal digital platform build (owned website, mailing list, archive, and release infrastructure; no rented audience). You never buy vague stewardship. You buy concrete structural outputs with set review milestones. 01 Ownership The client retains ownership of their work. The Studio retains its proprietary frameworks and licenses delivered framework materials for the client’s practice. Public-facing writing transfers to the client upon final settlement. 02 Availability & interventions The client triggers an intervention when it is needed. We agree response times, reserved capacity, and the scope of each intervention in advance. Periods of absence are part of the engagement, giving the artist room to work independently. Their consent and creative control remain explicit throughout. 03 Fees The subscription is paid monthly in advance for reserved availability across the agreed cadence. Project commissions carry a fixed fee. We agree additional scope before work begins. Read the full Terms of practice © 2026 Wild Lake Studio LLC. All rights reserved. Wild-Lake™ and associated mark systems are trademarks of Wild Lake Studio. All intellectual property, client frameworks, and editorial work remain under sovereign ownership agreements.

hasPart.name: The method: diagnosis & scope
hasPart.text: The manual The method: diagnosis & scope Traditional A&R and institutional pipelines can extract creative output faster than an artist's internal and operational infrastructure can carry it. Delivery demands then exceed the capacity required to sustain the work. Wild-Lake is the structural counterpart. We build the conditions, capacity, and artistic rigor required for work that endures. An engagement may be initiated by the artist or commissioned by a manager, label, gallery, or agency. The artist enters willingly and retains control of the work. The practice begins with the assets the artist already holds: raw material, rights, skills, audience relationships, and working infrastructure. We identify what those assets can support, agree an intervention, observe it in use, and revise it against the result. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share. hasPart.name: The mechanics of talent architecture
hasPart.text: The mechanics of talent architecture Talent architecture treats a career as an interdependent system of creative assets, working conditions, capacity, and commitments. The four orbital principles below define what we examine and how the artist builds durable career equity. 1. Core mass Condense the raw material before exposing it to market pressure. We protect studio time, research, rehearsal, and revision so the work develops density and artistic rigor. Market exposure follows material the artist can stand behind and infrastructure that can carry the response. 2. Orbital velocity Calibrate output to the artist's actual capacity. We examine the release schedule, workload, income requirements, and recovery time, then set working rhythms, access boundaries, and decision responsibilities. Capacity and delivery are reviewed together so output does not consume the person sustaining it. 3. Elliptical cycles Use both public and quiet phases intentionally. Perihelion describes periods of release, exhibition, production, and live performance. Aphelion describes research, rest, and raw gestation. We scope commitments and resources for each phase so quiet development contributes to the next body of work rather than being treated as failure. 4. Escape velocity Build enough independent capacity to leave predatory deals, reactive trends, and draining environments. Retained rights, direct audience relationships, and working infrastructure generate leverage without surrendering equity. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share, so the artist retains the assets and decisions required to change course.

hasPart.name: Execution: demolition, critique, honesty, cadence
hasPart.text: Execution: demolition, critique, honesty, cadence Controlled demolition Audit the practice with the artist. Identify the brittle systems, inherited commitments, and habits that exceed available capacity. Agree what to remove, retain, or rebuild, then establish working conditions that protect the artist's autonomy. Test the changes in actual work before treating them as settled. Critique & revision Study raw material closely across visual art, sculpture, installation, writing, music, film, and performance. Offer direct interpretations and revisions that the artist can test, use, or reject. Examine ego loops and dependence on external validation when they drain stamina or distort decisions. Evaluate changes through the work itself. Conversational brutalism Expose the load-bearing limits without euphemism: what the practice can carry, what it costs to deliver, and where commitments exceed available time, resources, or physical capacity. Make those conditions explicit so the artist can decide what changes and what support is required. Observation & absence Alternate high-density interventions with total absence from day-to-day execution. We observe, critique, and agree the intervention, then step back so the artist works without surveillance. At the next agreed review, artist and studio examine what happened and refine the intervention through use.

hasPart.name: Institutional alignment: managers, agents, labels & curators
hasPart.text: Institutional alignment: managers, agents, labels & curators Wild-Lake works with managers, booking agents, labels, galleries, curators, and A&R executives as a defensive buffer and developmental engine around the artist. We do not replace those roles. We examine how institutional demands affect the capacity, artistic rigor, and long-term value of the underlying creative asset. Before work begins, the artist, representative, and studio agree the scope, decision responsibilities, delivery timeline, access boundaries, and review points. The artist confirms participation and determines what material or information may be shared. A third-party commission creates no claim on the artist's work. When demands exceed capacity, we make the conflict explicit and revise the scope, resources, or timeline with the parties involved. Delivery is planned against actual conditions. Each review checks whether those boundaries hold, whether the intervention supports the work, and what must change to prevent over-extraction. What our involvement means Our judgment develops through sustained attention, critique, and working together. We can speak to the commitment to craft, care for the person sustaining it, and respect for ownership that we have encountered in that work. Curators, labels, publishers, producers, collectors, and institutions can draw on that account when considering a working relationship with the artist. We cannot guarantee an artist's future. Meet the artists and creators Governance & RACI Wild-Lake provides external critique and structural architecture, never competing authority. Before any institutional engagement begins, we establish a written governance map with the artist, management, and label defining who holds final sign-off across repertoire, visual direction, rollout, and touring.

hasPart.name: Artist wellbeing & development protocols
hasPart.text: Artist wellbeing & development protocols The pace, boundaries, and expectations of an engagement account for the artist's history, physical experience, and present capacity. The artist decides what to share and can pause, decline, or change direction at any time. We support artists rebuilding self-trust after narcissistic abuse, examining narcissistic patterns within themselves, or both. The work examines harmful relational patterns and establishes boundaries that protect creative autonomy. Trauma-informed pacing leaves room for care beyond the studio. During a retained engagement, Argelys may guide somatic, creative, or operational practices selected with the artist. Touch and co-regulation are optional and require explicit, ongoing consent. Participation in a practice is never a condition of retaining ownership or creative control. Outcomes & proof A healthy creative practice is measured in finished, durable output, not sentiment. Success looks like a coherent body of work, fewer abandoned projects, a release cadence the artist can sustain without burning out, and a live show built to survive a tour. Explore the practices Development protocols Active listening, structural honesty, automatic writing, grounding, movement, and vision quests, alongside operational systems for inquiries, communication, payments, and direct publishing. Each practice is optional. The artist can pause, decline, or change direction. Somatic and diagnostic exercises are optional tools deployed only when the work requires them, never a required curriculum. Protocols are tailored to the artist's physical schedule, conducted in-person in Brooklyn, remotely, in the studio, or on the road, in focused 60 to 90 minute working blocks. Explore the protocols →

hasPart.name: Ownership, Universe API & governance
hasPart.text: Ownership, Universe API & governance The artist retains 100% of their IP and creative control. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share. Asset-based leverage remains with the artist, including rights, income, and direct audience relationships. An upfront monthly Stewardship subscription reserves agreed capacity for client-triggered interventions. Scope, response windows, access limits, and review points are set before the engagement begins. Fixed commissions and focused advisory scopes are available when the work has a defined boundary. Universe API is Argelys's macro-micro diagnostic framework. It connects the conditions of the wider system with the artist's day-to-day capacity and decisions. It governs how interventions are scoped, tested in real conditions, and revised through use. Each intervention follows a closed loop: identify the constraint and the assets available, agree the change and the evidence to review, deploy it, observe its effect on the practice, and refine it with the artist. The review governs the next intervention and keeps the agreed scope proportional to the work. Next: engagements & pricing → · Terms of practice · Begin an engagement

Paid retainers from established artists and institutional partners directly fund higher-frequency Stewardship subscriptions for rising independent artists. That funding creates zero claim on the work, equity, or revenue of any artist supported. The practice funds this capacity through its own paid engagements rather than external capital or predatory backend deals. Within each engagement, upfront flat or recurring fees reserve asynchronous studio capacity and focused interventions. Interventions are followed by uninterrupted absence for independent execution. The artist retains 100% of their IP, masters, publishing, and direct audience ownership. At an agreed review, artist and studio examine the result and refine the next intervention. hasPart.name: Two rhythms, one practice
hasPart.text: Two rhythms, one practice The scope determines the rhythm: reserved availability with occasional intensive work, or higher-frequency support while building a foundation. Both reserve capacity for agreed interventions and protect time for independent execution. Established artists Retainer and intensive For established artists across disciplines, or their managers, labels, galleries, and agencies navigating touring, album cycles, exhibitions, or large-scale productions. Reserved availability The retainer reserves text and voice-note access to Argelys Samuel Oriach, Founder and artistic director, within agreed response windows. A capped number of urgent calls per quarter is agreed in writing. Wild-Lake provides structural advice, critique, and grounding. Day-to-day management and creative sign-off remain with the artist and their team. Focused intervention One-to-two-day intensives take place in person or remotely, spaced across months or years according to the work and the artist's capacity. Each intervention is followed by independent execution and an agreed review. Pre-session intake. A structural honesty audit, somatic and editorial work, and an infrastructure audit. A post-session structural memo recording observations, decisions, next steps, and the evidence to review. Pricing Retainer and intensive fees are agreed individually. Rising artists Subsidized Stewardship subscription Higher-frequency ongoing support for developing independent artists building foundational infrastructure. Established artist retainers underwrite the reserved capacity. Ongoing development Regular sessions on an agreed cadence, with independent execution between interventions. Optional Development protocols selected with the artist. Full Operational Infrastructure deployment within the agreed scope: request gating, static edge sites, direct payment routing, custom domain feeds, and async calendar boundaries. Scope and participation Eligibility rests on artistic rigor and structural need, with financial capacity factored in. Subsidized engagements are full working partnerships with mutual accountability. Artist and studio agree the scope, participation, boundaries, and review points before beginning, then assess the work and revise interventions together. Pricing A sliding scale based on need and available capacity, with the rate agreed individually.

hasPart.headline: Investigation. Experimentation. Invitation.

hasPart.name: Investigation. Experimentation. Invitation.
hasPart.text: About our founder Investigation. Experimentation. Invitation. Argelys Samuel Oriach · Founder & artistic director Argelys Samuel Oriach is a Dominican-born performance artist, artistic director, and systems architect based in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. He is the Founder and artistic director of Wild Lake Studio. He operates two laboratories: Seven Eighty Three (Lab 783), an independent systems design practice, and Wild Lake Studio, its research laboratory, which guides developing and independent artists. The studio operates from New York, Tampa, and Santiago, and works worldwide. Seven Eighty Three addresses macro-systems architecture. Wild-Lake works with the artist and the practice through sovereign A&R and talent architecture. Universe API unifies the two scales: identify the conditions, scope an intervention, observe it in use, and revise it against the result. Wild Lake Studio formalizes Argelys's fifteen-year independent practice. It began in his freshman year at Wesleyan University, when he was initiated into the Eclectic Society and started producing live shows, organizing cultural space, and working alongside artists. Across twelve or more multidisciplinary artists, that practice has combined structural stewardship, physical carrying capacity, and live production architecture. Personal website · LinkedIn

hasPart.name: The person and the work
hasPart.text: The person and the work Argelys builds infrastructure for artists on the same principles he applies to technical architecture: nothing decorative, and everything carries weight. He was born in the Dominican Republic to a mother who is a housekeeper and writer and a father who is a facility maintainer and musician. His structural impulse surfaced at eleven, when he taught himself 3D design software to draft his parents' dream home. An architect later used that file for construction. After the 2008 financial crash, he applied to Phillips Academy Andover to design the conditions of his own life on purpose. A method actor trained in the Alexander Technique, he spent the next sixteen years treating his body, voice, and daily life as a single structural instrument. In 2010 he attended Northwestern University's National High School Institute (Cherubs) theatre program and played Nick in a stage adaptation of The Handmaid's Tale. From there he studied somatic weight, posture, and human attention by inhabiting roles across institutions, physical staging, and corporate infrastructure. That foundation fueled a twelve-year trajectory building organic growth systems. He served as Cynthia Nixon's social media manager for her 2018 campaign for governor of New York, then moved to architecting sovereign digital frameworks from first principles. He went on to build brand infrastructure at VinePair, direct brand marketing at Kickstarter, and lead organic growth at CookUnity. He approached these corporate roles as an undercover durational performance: a calculated effort to build his life out of poverty while auditing how complex systems scale from the inside out. That cycle recently closed with an intentional return to his body, breath, and voice. Drafting, performance training, live production, and corporate growth gave him direct experience of both physical capacity and institutional scale. The studio applies that evidence to the conditions around the artist: what can be sustained, where the system exceeds its limits, and what must change.

hasPart.name: The creative practice & literary output
hasPart.text: The creative practice & literary output Performance governs how he works across writing, voice, movement, visual art, design, and acting for stage and screen. “Multidisciplinary” describes the range of media. “Performance artist” describes how he inhabits them. At Wesleyan he sang with Ebony Singers, studying African-American religious music through performance, including traditional and contemporary gospel, spirituals, and hymns. He also took African drumming courses. As a writer, he applies the same somatic and structural rigor to narrative in a maximalist, automatic, lyrical, stream-of-consciousness style. His focus remains the physical and digital mechanics beneath every medium. This Is Not a Love Story (Yankees) : a digital short, published at thisisnotalovestory.net. It is a screenplay written in prose form. Graduation : a debut autofiction novel (in progress). Untitled One-Act Play (in progress). Untitled Pilot (in progress).

hasPart.name: Education & critical archive
hasPart.text: Education & critical archive He majored in English at Wesleyan University, where he took extensive coursework in studio art and critical theory. His senior honors thesis was Breaking the circle of the plantation: Violence, affect and the ephemeral in Junot Díaz's Afro-Caribbean literary imagination. The thesis positions The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao as an alternative archive of the diaspora. It examines Díaz's Afro-Caribbean literary imagination through queer theory, performance studies, affect studies, and critical race theory.

hasPart.name: A personal framework
hasPart.text: A personal framework Argelys understands his approach through the architect and shaman archetypes. The architect gives the practice structure. The shaman attends to meaning, transition, and the artist's relationship to their work. Together they make him an alchemist, transforming raw material and lived experience into artistic form. These archetypes inform how he shapes the conditions around an artist while staying close to what the work means to them. He reflects on his approach through four terms. Investigation Understanding the foundations before proposing a structure. Asking what is present, what matters, and what the work needs. Experimentation Learning through making and lived experience. Letting what happens in practice inform the next decision. Emotional clarity Allowing time to understand a response rather than treating urgency as direction. Invitation Entering a creative relationship by mutual recognition and consent. Guidance is offered within a relationship the artist chooses.

hasPart.name: 00.0 // The myth of the 27 Club
hasPart.text: Culture treats the 27 Club like a romantic tragedy. It was a structural failure. When an artist breaks through without load-bearing infrastructure underneath them, visibility acts like dead weight stacked onto an unbraced frame. Labels, promoters, and press profit from immediate output, so they keep piling on tour dates, press cycles, and release deadlines. Nobody stops to pour concrete. Nobody builds the walls required to hold that pressure. And traditional representation rarely intervenes because percentage-based deals reward velocity. When a manager or agent takes twenty percent of gross revenue, their financial incentive is to keep the artist moving on the road, even while the artist's nervous system and creative practice are fracturing. Fame without architecture will always consume the person standing at the center of it. Sovereign infrastructure is what lets a generational artist survive their own success.

hasPart.name: Scope, consent & boundaries
hasPart.text: Scope, consent & boundaries Participation is voluntary. The artist controls pace, proximity, boundaries, and what they share. They can pause, decline, or change direction at any time. Consent is explicit, specific to the practice, and ongoing. Agreement to one practice does not authorize another. Wild-Lake operates as an artistic and structural practice rather than clinical therapy. These protocols support the conditions of making; clinical diagnosis and treatment sit outside the engagement. Trauma-informed pacing allows for the artist's history and present capacity, including rebuilding self-trust after narcissistic abuse or examining narcissistic patterns within themselves. Care beyond the studio remains available on the artist's terms. Before a protocol begins, artist and studio agree the constraint, the purpose of the intervention, the boundaries, and what they will observe. After use, they review its effect on the work and on capacity, then retain, revise, or stop it. The next intervention follows that evidence rather than a fixed program.

hasPart.name: Cognitive & editorial protocols
hasPart.text: Cognitive & editorial protocols These protocols develop artistic rigor and editorial precision. Each returns attention to specific material, decisions, and revisions the artist can evaluate. Active listening Listen before interpreting. The artist determines what to share and at what pace. We identify the question, distinguish observation from assumption, and check our understanding with the artist before proposing a change. Conversational brutalism Expose the load-bearing conditions directly: time, money, commitments, physical capacity, and the limits of the work. The conversation identifies what the practice can carry and what must change. The artist decides how to act on that information. Close reading Study selected texts and the artist's material for structure, language, form, and unresolved questions. Make editorial judgments specific enough to test through revision. Return to the revised work to assess what changed. Automatic writing Write continuously before editing to surface associations, images, and questions. Revisit the material afterward, identify what warrants development, and test it through deliberate composition or revision. Structured ideation Separate idea generation from evaluation. hasPart.name: Somatic & nervous system protocols
hasPart.text: Somatic & nervous system protocols These practices examine physical attention and nervous system capacity within the working relationship. The artist's reported experience governs the pace and whether a practice continues. Consensual co-regulation Use steady presence, active listening, and shared attention only within boundaries agreed with the artist. Discuss pace and proximity before beginning. Touch is optional and requires separate, explicit, ongoing consent. The artist can withdraw consent, pause, or end the practice at any time. Stillness & observation Make time to notice thoughts, sensations, and the working environment without requiring a particular state. The artist determines the duration and whether to continue. Review what the observation reveals about the conditions of making. Breath mechanics Bring gentle attention to breathing in relation to movement, voice, and concentration. The artist chooses the pace and stops or adjusts when needed. Observe whether the practice supports the specific task rather than treating a breathing pattern as a performance target. Self-directed & consented contact Self-directed contact can provide a point of physical attention. Any guided contact is discussed beforehand, including its purpose, location, and limits, and begins only with explicit consent. Consent remains ongoing; the artist can decline, change, or stop contact immediately. Participation never requires touch.

hasPart.name: Spatial & physical protocols
hasPart.text: Spatial & physical protocols Spatial and physical practices examine how environment, movement, and voice affect the work. Participation and intensity follow the artist's capacity rather than a predetermined outcome. Field immersion Change the environment to examine assumptions and working conditions. Field immersion can include vision quests, environmental displacement, and visits to a local park, the Blue Ridge Mountains, or Santiago and the surrounding campo , where Argelys's family is rooted. His experience of rural life and poverty grounds discussion of labor, access, and the material conditions that sustain creative work. Agree the setting, purpose, practical demands, and boundaries with the artist before a visit, then review what the change of environment reveals. Voluntary movement & rhythm Use movement or dancing to study rhythm, impulse, spatial relationships, and physical expression. The artist sets the intensity and duration. Relate observations back to the work or the conditions required to make it. Tension discharge Use voluntary shaking or other self-directed movement to notice and respond to held tension. The artist chooses whether to participate and how to move. Stop or adjust when requested and review whether the practice supports the task at hand. Vocal & emotional release Allow sound, tears, silence, or other expression without prescribing a response. Emotional release is optional and is never evidence required to demonstrate progress. The artist controls what is expressed and whether it becomes material for the work. Protocol format & cadence Somatic and diagnostic exercises are optional tools deployed only when the work requires them, never a required curriculum. Protocols are tailored to the artist's physical schedule, conducted in-person in Brooklyn, remotely, in the studio, or on the road, in focused 60 to 90 minute working blocks.

hasPart.name: Technical & boundary infrastructure
hasPart.text: Technical & boundary infrastructure These systems are the external armor protecting the internal capacity developed through cognitive, somatic, and physical work. Scope them to the actual demand on the artist's attention, income, access, or direct audience relationships. Programmatic request gating Close social media DMs to professional inquiries. Route requests to a structured Tally or Typeform form hosted on the artist's custom domain. Require project scope, a budget that meets the artist's minimum, and acknowledgment of terms before the inquiry reaches the inbox. Direct cold contacts to the form through saved replies or automated email responses. Review whether the gate admits relevant requests and protects the artist's attention. Single-file edge deployments Deploy portable static HTML and CSS directly to Cloudflare Pages on the artist's own domain. A single-file site can operate without a database, framework dependencies, or a build pipeline. Keep a portable source copy, test the published page, and revise it when the artist's requirements change. Async communication boundaries Close open calendar booking. Require a written agenda and decision brief at least 48 hours before a call is booked, including the specific question, relevant material, and decision needed. Book only when the purpose and scope are clear. Review whether calls resolve decisions and preserve time for independent execution. Direct payment routing Connect Stripe Payment Links to the artist's own Stripe account, with payouts tied directly to their bank account. Send links to buyers or embed them on the artist's site to bypass marketplace commissions. Payment processing fees still apply. Verify the payment and payout path, and keep the offer and customer relationship under the artist's control. Custom domain syndicate feeds Connect a Buttondown newsletter to the artist's custom domain through the required DNS records and publish a native RSS feed on the static site. Maintain exportable subscriber lists and publishing archives for direct audience relationships. Test subscription, delivery, feed access, and export so distribution remains usable beyond any platform. Universe API governs the shared loop: identify the artist's actual bottleneck, scope the intervention, deploy it in live conditions, observe the result, and revise it through use. Internal practices and technical systems are evaluated together so an external demand does not consume the capacity the artist has built.

hasPart.abstract: Artist wellbeing Development protocols Every protocol serves one structural objective: increasing the artist's capacity to sustain demanding creative work without dependency or burnout. Argelys Samuel Oriach, Founder and artistic director of Wild-Lake, guides the work within an agreed engagement. Internal regulation and external armor are two halves of one system. Cognitive rigor, nervous system capacity, and spatial movement support the person doing the work. Inquiry, publishing, payment, and communication systems protect that capacity from external demands. Each intervention addresses an identified bottleneck, is tested in practice, and is revised against what happens.
